newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rouble steady as c.bank keeps T-bills attractive.
newsitem.headline: Rouble steady as c.bank keeps T-bills attractive.

text.p: The rouble was steady on Thursday after central bank buying earlier this week kept the government bond market attractive, dealers said.

"The central bank realises that banks and investors may change their attitude towards Treasury bills and prefer dollar investments. This is why it has been raising its dollar rates during the last week more slowly," an Inkombank dealer said.
The central bank said it had set 5,333/5,373 as its bid and offer rates against the dollar on Thursday compared with Wednesday's 5,331/5,371.
Until the end of last week, the rouble was falling as much as nine points daily.
Dealers said the central bank bought roubles on Monday and Tuesday to support the T-bill market.
Roubles for today settlement were quoted at 5,364-67 per dollar, the same as in early trading. They were quoted at 5,367-68 late on Wednesday. Tomorrow roubles were steady at 5,366-69 per dollar.
Overnight rouble credits yielded 40-50 percent compared with Wednesday's late 20-50 percent.
The high rouble rates made it attractive to short the dollar briefly, taking advantage of the same rates on roubles for tomorrow and today settlement in the currency market.

"Given the current equality of the dollar rates, it is profitable now to sell dollars for today settlement, offer roubles for overnight credits and buy dollars back for tomorrow settlement," Neftekhimbank dealer Vladimir Zrazhevsky said.
